title: Sentinel-5P TROPOMI Level-2 Nitrogen Dioxide (NO2) Columns
description: Orbit-level (Level-2) retrievals of tropospheric, stratospheric and total NO2 vertical columns from the TROPOMI spectrometer on the Copernicus Sentinel-5 Precursor satellite, with near-daily global coverage at about 3.5 x 5.5 km (since 6 August 2019; 3.5 x 7 km before) and an early-afternoon overpass (about 13:30 local solar time).
purpose: Mapping NO2 pollution hotspots and trends over Algerian cities, ports, industrial zones, power plants and oil and gas facilities, as an air-quality hazard indicator where ground monitoring is sparse.

spatial_extent.description: Global, orbit-by-orbit swaths (~daily). Algeria must be extracted from individual orbit files or from gridded third-party Level-3 products.

temporal_extent.frequency: daily (one early-afternoon overpass per location; orbit files)
temporal_extent.description: Level-2 data available since April 2018 (CDSE). Timeliness streams: NRTI (near real time), OFFL (offline) and RPRO (reprocessed). A PAL reprocessing with processor v2.3.1 covers 1 May 2018 - 14 November 2021.

resolution.spatial: 3.5 x 5.5 km at nadir since 6 Aug 2019 (3.5 x 7 km before)

crs: Satellite swath geometry (pixel latitude/longitude and corner bounds, WGS 84)

variables.name: nitrogendioxide_tropospheric_column
variables.description: Tropospheric vertical column of NO2 (multiply by 6.02214e19 for molec/cm2)

variables.name: nitrogendioxide_tropospheric_column_precision
variables.description: Error estimate of the tropospheric column

variables.name: qa_value
variables.description: Quality assurance value; use > 0.75 for tropospheric columns (> 0.5 if cloudy scenes are of interest)

variables.name: averaging_kernel
variables.description: Averaging kernels for comparison with models or profiles

processing: Slant NO2 columns are retrieved by DOAS from TROPOMI UV-visible spectra and converted to vertical columns with a retrieval-assimilation-modelling system (DOMINO-2 / QA4ECV heritage) that uses the TM5-MP chemistry transport model to separate stratospheric and tropospheric parts and air-mass factors that depend on clouds (FRESCO-S) and surface reflectivity. Processor versions evolve (v01.x to v02.x), with version 2 increasing tropospheric columns for polluted scenes.
validation: Product Readme (PRF-NO2, v02.05.00, 2023-03-16): independent validation by the S5P Mission Performance Centre and Validation Team concludes that versions 02.02.00 and 02.03.01 of the NRTI/OFFL NO2 data are compliant with the S5P Cal/Val Plan requirements (tropospheric NO2: bias 25-50%, random error 0.7x10^15 molec/cm2). Up-to-date results are in the quarterly ROCVR validation reports (mpc-vdaf.tropomi.eu).
limitations: Column amounts, not surface concentrations; converting to ground-level NO2 requires modelling.
Only pixels with qa_value > 0.75 should be used for tropospheric columns; clouds, snow/ice and bright surfaces reduce valid coverage.
Processor version changes (v1 to v2, and later 02.0x updates) cause step changes; use reprocessed (RPRO/PAL) data for trend analysis.
Single early-afternoon overpass; does not resolve diurnal cycle.
Over bright desert surfaces and with dust aerosol, surface-reflectivity and air-mass-factor errors may be larger (AEO caution, not quantified for Algeria by the provider).

algeria_notes: Expected to show enhanced NO2 over Algiers, Oran and industrial/hydrocarbon sites (e.g. Arzew, Skikda, Hassi Messaoud), but signals must be averaged over weeks to months; this is an AEO expectation to be checked against data, not a provider statement.
